name: Question 2
problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & -8 \\ 2 & -2 & -4 \\ -2 & 6 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

The matrix above has eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=4,$ ${\lambda }_{2}=2,$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=0.$ Find a Jordan canonical form of the matrix.
worked_solution:
Notice that we are given a $3\times 3$ matrix that has precisely $3$ distinct eigenvalues. 

Therefore, $A$ is diagonalizable, and its Jordan canonical form is

$$
{J}_{1}(4)\,⊕\,{J}_{1}(2)\,⊕\,{J}_{1}(0)=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

**Note:** The Jordan canonical form is unique up to the order of the Jordan blocks.

Question 2

A=[40−82−2−4−264]

The matrix above has eigenvalues λ1=4, λ2=2, and λ3=0. Find a Jordan canonical form of the matrix.

a
[400021000]
b
[400020000]
c
[410021000]
d
[400021001]
e

Correct
EXPLANATION

Notice that we are given a 3×3 matrix that has precisely 3 distinct eigenvalues.

Therefore, A is diagonalizable, and its Jordan canonical form is

J1(4)⊕J1(2)⊕J1(0)=[400020000].

Note: The Jordan canonical form is unique up to the order of the Jordan blocks.
